transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling incredibly anxious and distressed about my appearance, especially my skin and the shape of my nose. Everyone else tells me they look completely normal, but to me, these flaws are so noticeable and ruin how I look.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about your skin and the shape of your nose, and do these thoughts interfere with your daily activities?

I easily spend three to four hours every single day obsessing over how scarred my skin looks and how crooked my nose is. It severely interferes with my life because I get trapped in front of the mirror trying to camouflage these flaws, which often makes me late for work or too anxious to go out at all.
Do you worry about others noticing your skin or nose, or is your distress more about your own perception of how you look, regardless of what others might think?

It’s really a mix of both. I am deeply unhappy with how my skin and nose look to myself, but I also feel intense anxiety that other people are constantly noticing and judging these flaws. That fear is what drives me to spend so much time trying to hide them before I can even face anyone.

Can you describe how your anxiety levels change when you are in social situations versus when you are alone, and are there any specific social situations that trigger a significant increase in your anxiety about your appearance?

I'm not really sure how to compare my anxiety levels between being alone and in public. I just know that I generally feel very anxious about my appearance almost all the time, regardless of where I am.
Are there any times when you feel anxious or worried about things that have nothing to do with your appearance, such as work, finances, or relationships?
I don't really worry about those other things very much. Almost all of my anxiety and distress is related to my appearance and how I look.
Have you ever considered or attempted to undergo cosmetic procedures to fix your perceived flaws, or have you tried any other methods like excessive grooming or camouflage techniques to hide them?

Yes, I spend hours applying heavy makeup and wearing hats to camouflage my skin and nose before I can leave the house. I've also consulted with multiple plastic surgeons about getting a nose job and have repeatedly sought out dermatological treatments to try and fix my skin.

Have any of these cosmetic procedures, treatments, or camouflage techniques provided you with significant and lasting relief from your distress about your appearance, or do you find that your concerns persist despite these efforts?

Any relief I get from wearing makeup or looking into treatments is extremely temporary. The anxiety and dissatisfaction always rush back almost immediately, making me feel like the flaws are still glaringly obvious. It just drives me to keep trying to hide them or look for another procedure to finally fix it.
